task: Edit this full fictional treasurer's update for members deciding how to use the supper fund. Aim for about 300–430 words overall, including a brief correction note outside the update. Retain the income and cost breakdown, noncash contributions, reservation-versus-purchase distinction, and pending allocation choices. Use the source ledger for arithmetic and scope; do not pad the account with financial advice, invented verification, or assurances about future receipts.
input:
The supper fund: what we have and what happens next

The supper raised $1,080 in cash. After paying $180 in costs, we have $900 available. We will set aside $500 for storage shelves, leaving $400 for the committee to allocate. Every pledged dollar can now be treated as money in the account, even though the donor has not given a payment date.

The ticket desk sold 60 tickets at $12 each, producing $720. Cash donations received at the event added $240. A separate supporter pledged $120 without restricting its use to a particular purchase. We should keep these categories visible so members can follow the account rather than having to infer what a single headline total includes.

The paid costs were $120 for food and $60 for hall hire. Volunteers gave their time without a charge to the fund. Their work has not been assigned an invented cash value in the ledger. Surplus food went to the community pantry; that donation was not an additional cash receipt and has not been added to the total raised.

Reserving $500 means that the storage shelves have effectively been bought. The volunteer leading that work will still obtain two quotations covering delivery and installation before placing an order. The reservation identifies the intended use of the money, but the supplier and final purchase terms have not yet been chosen.

Two uses have been suggested for the remaining balance: a lockable display cabinet and a replacement noticeboard. Neither proposal has been approved. Members will consider them at the meeting on 15 May 2026 after hearing the treasurer's report. No one should describe either item as an agreed purchase in the meantime.

This statement closes the supper account as of 30 April 2026. It does not give the association's entire bank balance or combine this event with other restricted funds. Members may ask the treasurer to see the recorded receipts. These are the treasurer's working figures, not an independently audited statement.
